title: Chana Aloo
subtitle: Chickpea and potato curry with cumin and tomato
excerpt: Tinned chickpeas and diced potato simmered in a spiced tomato base. A filling vegan weeknight curry that holds well and tastes better the next day.
sourceNotes: Anglo-Indian home cooking tradition. Classic combination of chickpea and potato in a dry-ish tomato masala.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight and reheat on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the batch easily. The curry improves with a day of rest in the fridge.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead. Reheat gently on the hob, adding a little water if it thickens too much.

content.text: Chana aloo is a simple chickpea and potato curry built on a spiced tomato base. It gives a filling, budget-friendly meal with very little effort. Watch the potato: it should be tender but not falling apart.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Stir often to stop it catching.
Stir in the garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the ground coriander, cumin, turmeric, and chilli powder. Stir for 30 seconds to coat the onion.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes. Add the potato cubes and salt. Stir well and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over a low heat for 20 minutes. Stir every 5 minutes to stop the base sticking.
Add the chickpeas. Cook uncovered for 5 more minutes until the sauce thickens and the potato is tender.
Stir in the garam masala. Taste and adjust salt. Scatter with fresh coriander if using.

items.symptom: The potato is still firm after 20 minutes.
items.cause: The potato cubes were too large or the heat was too low.
items.fix: Cut any large pieces in half and add a splash of water. Cook for another 5 to 10 minutes with the lid on.

items.cause: The tinned tomatoes were very liquid or the lid was kept on throughout.
items.fix: Remove the lid and cook over a medium heat for a few minutes to reduce the sauce.

items.symptom: The base caught and smells scorched.
items.cause: The heat was too high during the simmer.
items.fix: Do not scrape the bottom. Pour into a clean pan, add a splash of water, and continue on a lower heat.
